content.overview: Section 23 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the Central Government to delegate, by notification in the Official Gazette, such of its powers and functions under the Act (except the power to constitute an authority under s. 3(3) and to make rules under s. 25) as it may deem necessary or expedient, to any officer, State Government or other authority. Delegation supports decentralised implementation while retaining core legislative and certain constitutive powers at the Centre.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Was the power delegated by Gazette notification under s. 23? (2) Is the power within the non-delegable exceptions (s. 3(3) authority / s. 25 rules)? (3) Did the delegate act within the delegated scope?
content.study:
Delegation is limited by statute. Acts of a purported delegate outside the notification or within excluded powers are vulnerable.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Delegation power
sections.body: Central Government may, by Official Gazette notification, delegate powers and functions under the Act to any officer, State Government or other authority.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.body: Power to constitute an authority under s. 3(3) and power to make rules under s. 25 are not delegable under s. 23.

sections.heading: Scope control
sections.body: Delegate may exercise only what the notification entrusts; ultra vires action is open to challenge.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Enables practical administration and State/officer-level enforcement without surrendering core Central powers.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the notification, the power claimed, and whether it falls within a non-delegable exception.

examples.title: State-level direction
examples.body: If s. 5-type direction power is validly delegated to a State officer by Gazette notification, that officer may issue directions within the delegated scope.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Central Government delegate its s. 25 rule-making power under s. 23?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 23 expressly excepts the power to make rules under s. 25 from delegation.

distinctions.title: s. 23 delegation vs s. 4 appointment
distinctions.left: Delegates Central powers/functions by Gazette notification (with exceptions).
distinctions.right: Appoints officers and entrusts functions for Act purposes.

misconceptions.trap: All EPA powers can be freely delegated.
misconceptions.correction: s. 23 excludes constitution of authority under s. 3(3) and rule-making under s. 25.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Section 23 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Delegation by notification; exceptions (s. 3(3), s. 25); scope control.
